articles.title: Payment Gateway Timeout? How to Recover Transactions Without Charging Customers Twice
articles.excerpt: A customer clicks "Pay Now" during checkout. Your backend sends a payment request, but the gateway doesn't respond before the timeout expires. Your application displays an error. The customer clicks a…
articles.body: A customer clicks "Pay Now" during checkout. Your backend sends a payment request, but the gateway doesn't respond before the timeout expires. Your application displays an error. The customer clicks again. A few moments later, two payment attempts appear. This is one of the most dangerous mistakes in payment API integrations: treating a timeout as proof that a payment failed. When a payment request times out, the transaction may have succeeded, failed, or remained incomplete. Without a reliable recovery process, retrying can create duplicate charges, inconsistent order statuses, and unnecessary customer disputes. In this tutorial, we'll explain how to handle payment gateway timeouts, implement safe retries, verify transaction status, and design a recovery workflow using Node.js. 1.

articles.title: Semantic Retrieval for Travel Itinerary Planners: 3 Rules for Delete Semantics
articles.excerpt: Short answer: treat deletion as a retrieval contract, not as an embedding detail. For a travel itinerary planner, keep ingestion, query, and citation observable; use explicit collections and bounded c…
articles.body: Short answer: treat deletion as a retrieval contract, not as an embedding detail. For a travel itinerary planner, keep ingestion, query, and citation observable; use explicit collections and bounded candidate sets; and remove an itinerary item by its stable identity before it can reach the answer. This keeps a stale hotel or cancelled excursion from surviving merely because its wording still matches. The operational constraint is freshness. A planner can return a semantically perfect train connection that the user deleted ten minutes ago. I first thought increasing top_k would make the result safer. It made the opposite problem easier to see: duplicates and old snapshots occupied the candidate list, adding latency without adding useful choices.

articles.excerpt: If you walk into a room of engineers today and ask, “What is the purpose of software architecture?”, you will hear about scalability, modularity, defensibility, and clean code. They are equally right…
articles.body: If you walk into a room of engineers today and ask, “What is the purpose of software architecture?”, you will hear about scalability, modularity, defensibility, and clean code. They are equally right and largely missing the point. Architecture is not about art, and it is rarely about “perfection”. Architecture is a leverage mechanism whose only purpose is to give you control over the three bills you have to pay to keep a software organization alive. At its root, every technical decision you make is simply a trade-off between three specific costs. You can minimize one, maybe two, but never all three.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
articles.excerpt: Aldebaran looks for all the world like the brightest member of the Hyades star cluster. It isn't — and discovering why changes the way you look at constellations.
articles.body: For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth.
